source_review.notes: Checked primary MapReduce, Dryad, RDD, Naiad, Dataflow, and COST papers plus current official Spark and Flink documentation and Google SRE guidance. Sources support graph execution, movement/state/recovery trade-offs, competent baselines, unbounded-data semantics, task/shuffle/spill/state metrics, backpressure, and cause-oriented monitoring. All ten URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date.

evidence: Reviewed weighted graph span, resource demand/capacity bounds, cut movement/bandwidth bounds, edge movement tuple, state peak/integral, amplification, and streaming stability/catch-up notation.
Checked units, maxima versus sums, half-open state lifetimes, and explicit warning against double-counting movement already included in stage durations.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Work, elapsed time, span, movement, state peak, state occupancy, capacity, cost, and outcome remain dimensionally distinct.

evidence: Executed work-movement-state-ledger with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced 23-second span, 61 CPU-seconds, 15.25-second four-slot bound, 600,000,000 movement bytes, ten serialized movement seconds, 280,000,000-byte peak at second two, and all finish times.
Recomputed exercise one as 50-second span, 25-second CPU bound, and 50-second combined lower bound.
Recomputed movement ratios 1.5, 1.375, and approximately 0.917 plus 39,400 GB-hours and 900-GB simple peak.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Fixture durations, bandwidths, state lifetimes, and capacities are assumed inputs rather than empirical predictions.

evidence: Derived dependency span by maximum weighted path and resource lower bounds by conserved demand over usable service capacity.
Derived overall simple lower bound as a maximum rather than sum and retained conditions preventing overlap/double-counting errors.
Derived peak state as a maximum over simultaneous live objects, byte-time as an integral, and finite stream catch-up only when service exceeds arrival.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Lower bounds constrain but do not predict realized schedules.

evidence: Reviewed serial and parallel branches, one hot partition, aggregate versus cut capacity, local/remote movement, compressed/retried bytes, peak versus distributed state, and zero/low reuse.
Reviewed task failure, speculation, lost shuffle, corruption, checkpoint replay, reduced capacity, retry storms, backlog at service rates below/equal/above arrival, and moved bottlenecks.
Reviewed changed output semantics, late-data exclusion, approximation, shared-cost attribution, affected-population differences, and high-consequence degraded operation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Correctness and consequence bound the optimization space before performance comparison.

evidence: Traced result identity, physical graph, accepted/retry work, edge-local movement, state ownership/lifetime/durability, usable capacity, critical path, cost boundary, and retained evidence through examples and exercises.
Checked that totals, distributions, maxima, attempts, and graph versions are retained together.
Checked that each proposed optimization predicts cross-resource ledger changes and requires output/failure revalidation.
invariant_checking.notes: No utilization, average, byte count, scale curve, or price alone is treated as sufficient evidence.

evidence: Reviewed all ten ledger obligations from frozen outcome through consequence review.

Checked counterexamples for more-workers-always-faster, CPU-equals-wall, sum-all-durations, lower-bound-equals-runtime, nominal-equals-usable-capacity, all-bytes-equal, cache-equals-checkpoint, backpressure-equals-cause, average-equals-tail, and cheaper-equals-better claims.
Reviewed bottleneck diagnosis, controlled experiment, baseline, failure amplification, and streaming stability arguments.
proof_review.notes: Correctness, mathematical bounds, empirical causality, operational recovery, economic accounting, and domain approval remain separate obligations.

evidence: Audited uses of bound, prediction, required, useful, minimum, bottleneck, stable, correct, and prove.
Confirmed fixture outputs and arithmetic examples are scoped to stated assumptions and never labeled measured production performance.
